lean.statement: ∀ {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B] (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure A) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (K : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel A B) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel K] {δ : ℝ}, (∀ s : Set A, MeasurableSet s → |μ.real s - ν.real s| ≤ δ) → ∀ t : Set B, MeasurableSet t → |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (K ∘ₘ ν).real t| ≤ δ
approved_definition_context: A and B carry arbitrary sigma algebras. MeasureTheory.Measure A is a measure on the measurable space A. IsProbabilityMeasure ρ means ρ has total mass one. For a finite-mass event S, ρ.real S is its ordinary real measure, the toReal of its extended nonnegative measure.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel A B assigns a measure K x on B to each x in A and requires x↦K x T to be measurable for every measurable T. IsMarkovKernel K means every K x is a probability measure. K ∘ₘ ρ is the measure on B defined by integrating these transition measures against the input measure ρ.

MeasurableSet s says the subset belongs to the given sigma algebra. ∀ s followed by MeasurableSet s → quantifies over all measurable events. Absolute value and ≤ are ordinary real operations. There is no implicit topology, density, coupling or additional inequality assumed.
